stem: Jasper is a 2-year-old boy with asthma who presents with fever, hypoxia, focal right lower zone bronchial breathing, reduced air entry, crackles and dullness to percussion after a week of URI symptoms. Which one of the following is the most likely organism?
explanation: This presentation is most consistent with community-acquired bacterial pneumonia with a focal lobar examination in a febrile hypoxic child. In a 2-year-old, Streptococcus pneumoniae is the most likely organism.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Breathing difficulties

rationale: The question asks for the most likely organism causing focal pneumonia in a febrile toddler; the best answer is pneumococcus, here labelled as streptococcal pneumonia.

optionExplanations.A: Mycoplasma pneumoniae is more typical in school-aged children and adolescents.
optionExplanations.B: RSV commonly causes bronchiolitis in younger infants rather than focal lobar pneumonia.
optionExplanations.C: Human metapneumovirus can cause viral lower respiratory infection, but this focal lobar picture suggests bacterial pneumonia.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: Streptococcus pneumoniae is the commonest cause of community-acquired bacterial pneumonia in young children.
optionExplanations.E: Staphylococcus aureus can cause severe pneumonia, but it is less likely than pneumococcus in this scenario.

His vital signs are: RR 40/min, HR 150/min, Temp 39ºC and SaO
